description: Board M&A update covering the proposed acquisition of a distributed solar and storage platform.
provenance: Modeled on transaction committee materials for infrastructure and renewable-energy developers: strategic rationale, valuation bridge, diligence findings, funding, synergy plan, approval gates, and board resolution. Deliberately exercises an eight-slide mixed-pattern deck with a two-series valuation bar chart and transaction-specific financial detail.

content.title: Project Harbor — M&A Update
content.subtitle: Proposed acquisition of BrightSpan Energy | Board of Directors | September 8, 2026 | Strictly confidential

content.title: BrightSpan advances our distributed-energy strategy by three years.
content.subtitle: Transaction thesis
prose: The target owns or manages 684 MW of solar and 212 MWh of battery storage across 19 states.
Contracts cover 87% of FY2027 gross margin under PPAs or long-term service agreements.
Management recommends a $742M enterprise value and a $28M permitting escrow.

content.title: Offer value remains below comparable transactions
content.subtitle: Enterprise value to forward EBITDA; announced distributed-energy acquisitions

content.title: Confirmatory diligence — strengths and residual issues
content.subtitle: Workstreams completed through September 4, 2026

content.title: Funding and balance-sheet impact
content.subtitle: Sources, uses, and covenant headroom at expected December 2026 close
bulletPoints: Uses: $588M equity purchase, $126M debt assumed or refinanced, $18M fees, and $10M initial integration reserve
Sources: $238M Solstice cash, $210M new term loan, $170M infrastructure co-invest, and $124M seller rollover
Pro forma net leverage of 4.2x at close versus 5.0x covenant; expected below 3.5x by Q4 2027
No public equity issuance required; planned FY2027 development capital remains fully funded
Interest-rate hedge locks 70% of new term-loan exposure at an all-in 5.6% through 2029
Dividend policy unchanged; share repurchases paused until net leverage returns below 3.75x

content.title: Integration plan and value capture
content.subtitle: Day 1 through the end of FY2027
bulletPoints: Day 1 — retain BrightSpan brand and operating leadership; finance, treasury, and risk move to Solstice controls
First 100 days — consolidate procurement for modules, inverters, insurance, and O&M; target $12M annualized savings
Q2 2027 — migrate fleet monitoring to Solstice Atlas while preserving customer portals and dispatch protocols
Q3 2027 — combine development origination teams by region and introduce BrightSpan storage to 41 Solstice C&I customers
Q4 2027 — refinance four asset-level facilities; expected annual interest savings of $9M
Year three — $34M run-rate synergies: $21M cost, $8M financing, and $5M cross-sell contribution

content.title: Authorize signing at $742M with the full $28M escrow.
content.subtitle: Approval subject to final tax-equity consents and execution of committed financing
prose: Management returns if either New York upgrade estimate exceeds $35M.
A price adjustment may proceed if downside IRR remains above 11%.
